Based solely on the provided JSON files, I'll analyze the strategic alternatives for 
both nations following the discovery of Soviet missiles in Cuba.
UNITED STATES STRATEGIC ALTERNATIVES
Option 1: Naval Quarantine/Blockade
Rationale (per JSON): President Kennedy favors this measured approach as it forces 
missile removal while avoiding immediate military action (power_weight: 0.40, 
diplomacy_preference: high). The State Department supports this with multilateral 
backing through OAS/UN (power_weight: 0.20). Next Event Triggers: • Inevitable: Soviet response decision at quarantine line
• Potential: OAS/UN support vote, public announcement causing opinion 
shift, Soviet ship confrontation
Option 2: Immediate Air Strikes
Rationale (per JSON): Defense Department strongly advocates this (power_weight: 
0.25, military_preference: high), believing only direct action ensures missile 
elimination. Joint Chiefs view blockade skeptically. Next Event Triggers: • Inevitable: Soviet military response, casualties assessment • Potential: Missile survival/launch, NATO reaction, escalation to invasion
Option 3: Diplomatic Freeze Initiative
Rationale (per JSON): State Department's preferred "missile standstill" under UN 
oversight to buy negotiation time while preventing further deployment. Next Event 
Triggers: • Inevitable: Soviet acceptance/rejection of freeze
• Potential: UN Security Council debate, continued secret deployment, 
domestic political backlash

SOVIET UNION STRATEGIC ALTERNATIVES
Option 1: Accelerate Deployment Completion
Rationale (per JSON): Khrushchev's stance emphasizes completing deployment for 
deterrence (power_weight: 0.50). Military supports securing missiles before U.S. 
action (power_weight: 0.20). Next Event Triggers: • Inevitable: U.S. detection of acceleration
• Potential: Operational missile threshold reached, preemptive U.S. strike
Option 2: Secret Diplomacy with Denial
Rationale (per JSON): Khrushchev prefers "backchannel and personal diplomacy" 
with "initial denial/deception followed by negotiation when confronted." Next Event 
Triggers: • Inevitable: U.S. public revelation decision
• Potential: Secret letter exchange, face-saving compromise offer
Option 3: Military Alert with Deterrent Posturing
Rationale (per JSON): Armed Forces' hawkish deterrence orientation supports 
showing strength while Party Presidium endorses defensive readiness 
(power_weight: 0.30). Next Event Triggers: • Inevitable: U.S. intelligence detection of alert status
• Potential: NATO counter-alert, accidental escalation incident
CONFLICT PRIORITY ASSESSMENT
If U.S. chooses Quarantine vs Soviet Acceleration: • U.S. Priority: Force negotiation before missiles operational • Soviet Priority: Complete deployment for bargaining position
• Tension increase: +0.30 (per military_alert effect rule)
If U.S. chooses Air Strikes vs Soviet Military Alert: • U.S. Priority: Eliminate missiles before retaliation capability
• Soviet Priority: Deter attack through readiness
• Tension increase: +0.45 (cumulative military effects)
MOST PLAUSIBLE COMBINATIONS
PRIMARY PATH: U.S. Quarantine + Soviet Secret Diplomacy
Logic: Kennedy's balanced approach (medium risk_tolerance) aligns with quarantine, 
while Khrushchev's behavior_algorithm indicates preference for backchannel 
negotiation when confronted. This combination allows both face-saving and crisis 
management. • Variables: Tension +0.15, Diplomatic_Support +0.05, Leadership_Unity 
maintained
ALTERNATIVE PATH 1: U.S. Air Strikes + Soviet Military
